items.headline: 10-year G-Sec yield climbs to 7.48%, its highest since October 2022, on crude and US yields
items.summary: Up from 7.47% on Friday and 7.19% before the RBI hike. The rupee traded between 94.91 and 95.27 per dollar. Analysts see 7.4–7.8% over the coming months. Escalating.
items.rationale: Four-year-high yields lift borrowing costs for the government, companies and home buyers and erode banks' bond portfolios as oil and global rates keep pressure on.

items.headline: Brent settles 0.8% lower at $115.81 as Qatar, Saudi, Turkey and Pakistan hold talks in Tehran
items.summary: Peace hopes trimmed prices, though Iran's Guard declared the strait closed and attacks on Saudi Arabia continued. Still near six-month highs after $117.38 on Friday. Easing slightly.
items.rationale: Mediation offers a path to lower oil, but crude near $116 still keeps India's import bill, fuel costs and inflation high.

items.headline: US president says it is 'decision time' on Iran: a deal or strikes to 'finish it off'
items.summary: Iran wants seven conditions met before talks and says it is preparing a response to any strike. Reports say the US military could launch a major operation within 96 hours if ordered. Escalation risk.
items.rationale: A strike would likely push oil sharply higher and hit Indian equities, the rupee and bonds; a deal would bring the biggest relief.

items.headline: Foreign investors sell ₹1,462 crore; domestic funds buy ₹2,610 crore
items.summary: Selling resumed after Friday's buying day; foreign funds hold about 2.77 lakh net short index futures. October outflows already exceed ₹51,000 crore. Ongoing.
items.rationale: Continued foreign selling and short positions weigh on heavyweights and the rupee; domestic buying cushions the market.

items.headline: High tanker rates make Russian oil unviable for a state refiner in November; Gulf discounts lure buyers
items.summary: Record freight wipes out the Russian discount, so Indian refiners are turning to discounted Gulf cargoes where available. Escalating shift.
items.rationale: Losing cheap Russian barrels raises India's average crude cost and leans more on Gulf supply exposed to Hormuz risk.

items.headline: October sets a record of 28 attacks on Hormuz shipping; Iran says 'illegal routes' will soon be blocked
items.summary: Another tanker was disabled in the strait. Iran's oil keeps flowing while Gulf neighbours' exports are shut. Escalating.
items.rationale: Rising attacks and new route threats keep insurance, freight and delivered crude and LNG costs at records for India.

items.headline: Saudi–Houthi de-escalation ends; Saudi Arabia plans an assault to break the Red Sea chokehold
items.summary: The two sides exchanged attacks in the Gulf and Red Sea, and Red Sea war-risk insurance is rising. Escalating.
items.rationale: A wider war threatens Saudi crude bound for India and the Red Sea route for Indian exports to Europe, adding to freight costs.

items.headline: Suez Canal records its highest monthly ship tonnage since December 2023
items.summary: Egypt's cabinet reported the rise even as Houthi threats persist in the Red Sea. Partial easing for trade routes.
items.rationale: More ships using Suez would shorten routes for Indian exports to Europe and trim freight costs, if Red Sea security holds.
